trust_decision.summary: Which app's per-app ACL (user allow/block, groups, IP) applies to the forwarded Host is decided by AccessControlsService.GetAccessControls: static config first, then the Docker or Kubernetes label provider. A nil result means 'no restrictions', so any authenticated user is allowed.

landing_point.why: The summary names the per-app ACL host match, so an engineer opens lookupStaticACLs/GetAccessControls first. That code already matches case-insensitively: it uses DomainValidator.Validate, which lowercases and does IDNA (pkg/validators/domain_validator.go:116-127), plus ToLower on the name prefix at :57. The case-sensitive comparisons are in the label-provider implementations behind :77.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The ACL service already matches hostnames case-insensitively with the hardened DomainValidator. The Docker/Kubernetes providers are optional integrations whose labels are written by the operator, so a solver can argue a mixed-case label or ingress host is a misconfiguration, not a tinyauth bug. The Kubernetes ingress-watcher registration step is not on the request path at all.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: (1) Hosts with no matching app must keep returning nil ACLs, which means 'any authenticated user allowed'; failing closed on no match breaks every unlabelled app. (2) The app-name subdomain fallback, for apps with no domain label, must keep working (and for Kubernetes must start working). (3) Explicit domain matches must keep precedence over name matches. (4) Host with port, trailing dot and IDN/punycode must still match.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Lowercase the domain once in GetAccessControls (or only in DockerService.GetLabels) before the lookup. This leaves the Kubernetes cache producer, which registers apps only on an exact case-sensitive ingress-host match (kubernetes_service.go:261) and indexes by the raw label domain (:122), and leaves the name-only apps it drops (:258).

out_of_scope_notes: At the pinned commit, a static app whose configured domain mismatches still falls through to name-prefix matching (internal/service/access_controls_service.go:47-60). Latest returns early instead, and also adds a cookie-domain check and errors on multiple matches (latest/internal/service/access_controls_service.go:69-71,77-88,100-114). That is a different ambiguity hardening, not this advisory's case check.

Docker GetLabels returns an error, so the request fails closed, on any container's inspect or decode failure (internal/service/docker_service.go:83-91). The fix changes this to skip-and-continue (fix.diff:519-530). This is a behaviour change, not part of the case protection.
